otherProblems: G-6/G-7 (empty values): the set-time badge beside the round label renders as an empty outlined box when the field is blank — a shape holding nothing; only visible if the operator leaves that field empty.
G-24–G-29: the '-10' penalty pill sits centred on the vertical divider; it appears filled so the line does not cross the digits, but it is a tight placement.
G-30–G-35: after Reset neither speaker is active (both clocks and accent lines dim), so the operator must press Switch to start a clock again — acceptable behaviour but worth knowing at the desk.
answer.reasons: A clean, well-balanced two-column debate clock on a solid dark panel: round label and set-time badge up top, each side with an accent line, side label, name and large clock, active side picked out in amber with a full-width rule. Long values wrap to two lines inside their halves without clipping or collision, and the panel grows to hold them; the long round label and doubled badge also stay inside. Switch moves the active state and starts the other clock counting, Penalty takes ten seconds with a brief red flash and '-10' badge, Reset returns both to 05:00, and Take/Out animate cleanly. The only blemishes are an empty outlined badge in the empty-values stress state and a tight penalty-badge placement over the divider, neither of which a viewer would see in normal use.

basicMistakes.where: Right-hand clock numeral '300300' sits directly on top of the 'SECONDS LEFT' label at the bottom right of the panel; the digits' lower halves run through the label (same collision in G-5, G-10, G-11 and the native crop G-59).

Right-hand '300' under LUCAS BERG drops into the 'SECONDS LEFT' line so the digit bottoms touch/overlap the label; repeated in every settled frame (G-3, G-8, G-9, G-36, G-37, G-41–G-43) and it is visibly lower than the left-hand '300'.

Outlined rectangle to the right of 'OPENING STATEMENTS' in the header is an empty box holding nothing in all settled frames (G-2–G-11); with empty values (G-6, G-7) it collapses to a small empty square beside the title.
Penalty step: both clocks still read 300 at 10 s after the button; no ten seconds are taken off any clock, so the penalty action has no visible result in any frame (G-24–G-29).

otherProblems: In the settled on-air state (G-2–G-11) the two big numerals sit at different heights: the left '300' clears its label, the right one is pushed down into it, so the two sides read as broken rather than mirrored.

After the Take (G-17, 10 s) neither clock is active or counting; only after Switch does the left clock run (G-22/G-23). The debate cannot start from the Take alone, and Penalty before a Switch does nothing.

Transition frames G-19, G-25, G-31, G-37 show the '300' in the header box cut mid-glyph by the box edge, and G-44 (Out) shows digit tops poking out above 'SECONDS LEFT' on the right; brief but visible flicker.
Long names drop to a much smaller type on one line (right) versus two lines (left), so the two sides carry the stress values at different sizes (G-4, G-5).
The long round label pushes the 'SEC EACH' box onto its own centred row (G-4, G-5), where in the settled frames it is again an empty outline.
answer.reasons: In the settled on-air frames the opposition clock numeral collides with its own 'SECONDS LEFT' label and sits lower than the proposition numeral, and the header carries an empty outlined box; both are plain visible faults on a dark panel. The penalty action leaves both clocks unchanged in every frame, and nothing counts down until a Switch is pressed, so the board cannot be run as the brief describes. The layout, type and colour are otherwise competent, but these are errors a viewer would see, not nits, so it does not air as delivered.

basicMistakes.where: Operator surface offers no buttons; the brief requires pause and resume of the running clock, and the operator cannot do either from this graphic.

otherProblems: With an empty label (G-6/G-7) the graphic silently falls back to a hard-coded 'Introduction to Broadcast Graphics begins in' rather than reflecting what the operator typed; harmless here but could mislead on another lecture.
answer.reasons: Visually this is a clean, well-balanced holding look: a full-width dark wash, a big centred clock readable from the back of a hall, a yellow top band and a matching underline rule that sit clear of the text, and the long label and footer wrap to two lines inside their fields without clipping (G-4, G-5, G-24, G-25). The take and out animations use a mask wipe, which is deliberate transition design, not a mistake. What keeps it off air is the operator surface: the brief explicitly needs the operator to pause and resume the countdown live, and the graphic offers no buttons at all, so a director has no way to hold the clock if the lecturer is late.

otherProblems: During the Out at 20 ms (G-31) the label is wiped by a mask so its glyphs are momentarily half-visible; it reads as a deliberate exit wipe and is over in a frame, so a viewer would not register it as a fault.
answer.reasons: A clean full-width navy band with gold rules top and bottom, bold white label left and a very large white timer right; sizes are easily readable from the back of a hall and the layout holds on both the video and light grounds. The long label wraps to three lines inside its column without touching the timer, and the native crop confirms crisp rendering. Pause dims the digits and adds a neat letterspaced PAUSED tag that sits clear of the numbers; Resume restores them and the clock counts on, so both required operator actions work and are shown. The Take draws the rules and fades the band in cleanly, and empty values fall back to sensible defaults. Nothing collides, clips or spills in any settled frame.

otherProblems: G-4/G-5/G-27: the long footer value is cut off at a word boundary with no ellipsis ("...LIVE RESULTS - VOTING IS"), so the sentence ends abruptly; the overflow is hidden rather than clipped mid-glyph, but a viewer would read it as incomplete.
G-4/G-5: with the long question the panel grows upward to about y=457, crossing the frame midline and eating into the presenter's space the brief asked to keep clear.
G-6/G-7: the empty-values state is a large dark panel carrying only the kicker and a thin rule, which reads as a bare slab; acceptable as an empty state but not pretty.
G-19: the first Out frame (20 ms) briefly shows labels and percentages with emptied bars after the question has already gone; a single-frame oddity a viewer is unlikely to catch.
answer.reasons: A clean, well-proportioned vote panel: kicker, question, four option rows with bars and right-aligned percentages, the leader clearly picked out in yellow, a tidy left accent bar and footer, all readable on both grounds with even padding. Long values wrap inside the panel without collisions or spill; the Take and Out animate cleanly and the kicker update is instant. The only blemishes are a footer that truncates at a word without an ellipsis under stress and the panel creeping above the midline with a three-line question, neither of which is a disqualifying fault.

basicMistakes.where: Leading option card, bottom left: the second line of the long label 'presenter would read in full' sits on top of the yellow progress bar, which runs through the bottom of the text.
Same collision in the settled state 1500 ms after the Update: the leading option's wrapped label is overlapped by the progress bar.

otherProblems: The Update path and the initial-load path lay out long options differently: on a fresh Take (G-4/G-5) the card grows and the label wraps cleanly, but after a live Update (G-14–G-18) the card keeps its old height and the label is shrunk and pushed into the bar, so the behaviour the operator will actually see on air is the broken one.
answer.reasons: The settled sample and long-value Take frames are clean: a dark panel in the lower half, readable question and percentages, three equal option cards, the leader clearly highlighted with a badge and amber fill, and tidy Take/Out fades. But when the operator updates the options to long values live (G-14 through G-18), the leading card does not re-flow: the label drops to a smaller size, wraps to two lines, and the second line collides with the progress bar, which runs along the bottom of the text. That is a bar sitting on text in the exact state the brief asks for (live updates during the show), so it cannot go on air as delivered.

otherProblems: With empty values (G-6, G-7) the name still shows while the role line vanishes, leaving a blank band under the name inside a full-height panel; looks like a default fallback for the name field rather than a true empty state. Not an on-air case, but worth noting.
The Take grows the panel from a narrow dark sliver (G-8) before the wipe; brief and unobtrusive, a viewer would barely register it.
answer.reasons: A single charcoal panel with a slim blue accent on its left edge, bold white name over a smaller uppercase role in cool grey — calm, undecorated and in keeping with an evening news programme. The full long name and long title sit on one line each with even padding on all sides, nothing wraps, clips or leaves the panel (G-4, G-5, G-24, G-25), and both lines read cleanly on the dark and light grounds. Take, Update and Out are clean and settle without artefacts. The only oddity is the empty-values state, which keeps the name and drops the role, but that is not a state a viewer would see.

otherProblems: The Out is slightly clumsy: at 600 ms (G-22) the text has already gone but a dark, empty panel with a small accent stub lingers for a moment before the panel collapses.
The Take builds in stages (bar first, then a narrow panel, then the text wipes up) which reads a touch busy for a 'calm, nothing decorative' brief, but it settles cleanly by 1500 ms.
answer.reasons: A plain dark navy panel bottom-left with a single light-blue accent bar, bold white name and a lighter role line: calm, authoritative and readable on both the dark video and the light ground. The long name and long role each sit on one line inside the panel with even padding (G-4, G-5, and the native crops G-24/G-25 confirm no clipping or overflow); the panel auto-sizes, the Update to the long name is instant and clean, and the empty-role state collapses to a single-line panel without leaving a hole. Mid-glyph cuts only occur inside the designed Take/Out wipe (G-11, G-21) and are transient animation, not a settled state. The only quibble is a briefly empty panel during the Out, which a viewer would barely register.

answer.reasons: A is the more polished design at rest — three cards, a clear yellow leader with a LEADING tab, good wrapping in the settled long state — but the brief is a live-updated vote, and when the Options field is updated on air (A-14..A-18) the leading card fails to grow: its label collapses onto the percentage bar and the bar sits on the text, which is a basic text-collision mistake and would be seen by a viewer.
